title: Jyothi Surekha Gets Hero's Welcome After Archery Gold With Record-Equaling Score
excerpt: India's women's compound team beat China 238-234 in the Asian Games final at Aichi-Nagoya, matching a 12-year-old world record — the 30-year-old veteran's fourth Asiad gold.
body:
• India's women's compound archery team — Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep — beat China 238-234 in the September 30 final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, retaining the Hangzhou gold.
  • The 238-point total equalled the world record for a 24-arrow women's compound team match, set by South Korea at the 2014 Incheon Asian Games.
  • It is Jyothi's fourth Asian Games gold and a first Asiad gold for her teammates, 21-year-old Chikitha and 18-year-old Prithika.
  • India edged South Korea 234-233 in the semifinal earlier the same day; PM Narendra Modi congratulated the trio on X, calling the feat "tremendous."

Jyothi Surekha Vennam has come home from the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games to a hero's welcome. The Indian women's compound archery team — Jyothi, 21-year-old Chikitha Taniparthi and 18-year-old Prithika Pradeep — beat China 238-234 in the September 30 final with a world-record-equaling 238, defending the title India won in Hangzhou.

A final won arrow by arrow

India took control from the first rotation at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square, opening 30-28 and never letting go. The trio's 24 arrows — 22 of them reportedly in the 10-ring — posted 238, matching the world record South Korea set at Incheon 2014. China stayed close through the third end but faltered with two nines in the final rotation while India held its nerve with perfect 10s.

https://x.com/Telugu360/status/2107085265588380093

Earlier in the day, the trio had edged South Korea 234-233 in a one-point semifinal — two 10s from Chikitha and Prithika and a nine from Jyothi making the difference at 175.

Speaking to ANI after the final, Jyothi said the team had reminded each other to give their best and focus on the next shot.

"We are very happy. Today was our first medal match in archery, and we won gold. It feels really good because as a team, we have worked very hard. In both the semi-final and final matches, we gave our best effort and gave 100 per cent."

— Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Indian compound archer

The context: India's compound archery run

Compound archery is not the Olympic recurve discipline — the compound bow's pulley system makes it more stable and accurate, so scores crowd the 240-point maximum and matches turn on a single arrow. India has medaled in the women's compound team event at every Asian Games since its introduction in 2014: bronze in Incheon, silver in Jakarta 2018, and gold in Hangzhou 2023 and now Aichi-Nagoya. Jyothi, 30, is the one constant across those campaigns.

At Hangzhou she became the first Indian archer to win multiple Asian Games golds, sweeping the women's individual, women's team and mixed team titles. Her Nagoya gold is her fourth at the Asian Games — and a first for debutants Chikitha and Prithika, an 18-year-old from Nagercoil who shot like a veteran herself.

What this gold means

It was India's seventh gold of these Games, and it tells a larger story: six of the seven have come in team events, the only individual gold belonging to trap shooter Neeru Dhanda. Harmanpreet Kaur's women's cricket team opened the rush on September 22; the men's compound team defended its title the same day, and Chikitha returned hours later to win the mixed team gold with Sahil Jadhav in a shoot-off against South Korea. The pipeline, not just the podium, is working.

PM Narendra Modi congratulated the trio on X, calling the feat "tremendous." Ministers Pralhad Joshi and Kiren Rijiju followed, with Rijiju writing that they had "shot the arrows perfectly" under the #Cheer4Bharat banner.

"A Gold for India! Congratulations to Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Prithika Pradeep and Chikitha Taniparthi on winning the Gold Medal in the Women's Compound Team event at the Asian Games 2026. This is even more special because their performance also equalled the World Record."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, on X

Diaspora angle

For Indians abroad, this is the kind of gold that travels fast across group chats: a world record, equaled, against China, in a sport India has quietly owned for a decade. Jyothi has won on American soil too — the Women's Open Pro title at the Lancaster Archery Classic in Pennsylvania in 2022 — and her arc, from a swimmer who took up archery at 11 to one of India's most decorated archers, is a story the diaspora loves to claim.

What's next

The Nagoya archery program still has medals to decide, with Chikitha — who topped the compound women's individual qualification with a career-best 705 — among the contenders. Beyond the Games, the World Cup and World Championship calendar awaits, with India now the team everyone else measures itself against. For Jyothi, the target is simple: keep the run going. For Chikitha and Prithika, Nagoya announced that the next generation has already arrived.

The trio beat China 238-234 in the final, matching the world record set by South Korea in 2014.
